title: Grill v1 Typst Zettelkasten architecture
details: Outcome: reach shared agreement on the version-one architecture for a self-contained Typst Zettelkasten, its Rust CLI/LSP, and Neovim integration. Boundary: design only; no implementation. Deferred: controlled vocabulary and category policy, templates, export/publication, structural roles, and performance-dependent Tinymist adaptations. Decisions reached so far: one closed archive boundary; zettel/*.typ absolutely flat; IDs and filenames use YYMMDDHHmm with collision moved to the next minute; canonical metadata is visible Typst markup; baseline file shape uses explicit archive-local lib import, #show: zettel, '= TITLE <ID>', required but possibly empty #abstract, keywords/category markup, and literal ten-digit @ID links; all Zettel use one structural type; lib is user-owned presentation code under hardcoded v1 semantic contracts; single Rust executable provides CLI and companion LSP; Neovim plugin is thin; no Zettel compilation or archive compilation in core scope; source-format migrations are explicit; filename existence defines identity even when content is malformed; graph edges come only from literal @ID AST nodes; no persistent metadata or graph cache, with CLI/LSP rebuilding in-memory metadata and relation tables from source; lib neutralizes ten-digit refs for Tinymist while zk lsp owns Zettel completion, validity, navigation, backlinks, and display. Completion evidence: human approval of a consolidated design, then docs/PROJECT.md, docs/DESIGN.md, and relevant decision records are written and the slice is marked done.

Deferred: controlled vocabulary and category policy, templates, export/publication implementation, structural roles, full dependency-resolution compilation, and performance-dependent Tinymist adaptations. Completion evidence: human approval of a consolidated design; docs/PROJECT.md, docs/DESIGN.md, decision records, and research notes reflect it; slice marked done.
